Ladakh sterilizes over 2,950 dogs to protect Black-necked Cranes

In Ladakh, over 2,950 free-ranging dogs have been sterilized as part of an initiative to protect the vulnerable Black-necked Crane. The Black-necked Crane is the state bird of Ladakh and a cultural symbol, listed globally as "vulnerable." Fewer than 100 of these cranes are estimated to survive in India, with the global population around 11,000-12,000, primarily on the Tibetan Plateau. The sterilization effort aims to safeguard the remaining crane population and other wildlife in the region.
